title: Green Smoothie
subtitle: Spinach, banana, and apple blended with oat milk, bright and clean-tasting
excerpt: A blender breakfast that comes together in five minutes: baby spinach, frozen banana, eating apple, and oat milk. Bright green, naturally sweet, and satisfying enough to carry you through a busy morning.
sourceNotes: Green smoothies became a mainstream breakfast category in the early 2010s, popularised by raw-food and wellness communities. This version uses everyday supermarket ingredients.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Pre-portion spinach, banana, and apple into freezer bags and blend straight from frozen with the oat milk, no prep on the morning itself.

content.text: A green smoothie is a blender breakfast you can make faster than toast. Spinach goes in with almost no detectable flavour once the banana and apple are doing their job. That makes it a reliable way to get iron and folate into a morning routine without much effort. The colour is vivid and unambiguously green. The taste, though, is mild, sweet, and refreshing. The one thing you cannot skip is a frozen banana. It gives the smoothie a thick, milkshake-like body that a fresh banana simply doesn't achieve.

items.prepNote: cored and roughly chopped, no need to peel

content.text: Put the {{spinach}} spinach into the blender jug first, this keeps it closest to the blade and ensures it blends fully rather than staying in leafy clumps. Add the {{banana}} banana chunks, the {{apple-eating}} apple (skin on is fine; it adds a little pectin), the {{lemon-juice}} lemon juice, and then pour the {{oat-milk}} oat milk over the top. The liquid goes in last so the blender has something to work with immediately.

Blend on high for 45 to 60 seconds. Scrape down the sides if needed, then blend for another 15 seconds. Taste: if it needs sweetness, add the {{honey}} honey and blend briefly to combine. Pour immediately, green smoothies separate quickly on standing and are at their best the moment they're made.
Swap half the apple for half a cucumber. Lighter in flavour and very cooling in warm weather.
Stir in a tablespoon of nut butter after blending for a longer-lasting breakfast with more staying power.
A thumbnail of fresh ginger blended with the spinach adds warmth and works particularly well with apple.
Almond milk makes this slightly thinner; coconut milk makes it richer and tropical. Whole cow's milk works too if you're not dairy-free.

The most practical version of this recipe is the freezer-bag approach: portion out the spinach, banana chunks, and apple into individual zip-lock bags and freeze. On the morning, tip a bag straight into the blender, add the oat milk, and blend. No measuring, no chopping, just pour. The bag method also means there's no fresh produce to go off if your week gets busy.
